In DNA, the synthetic base vexanine pair.why: Vexanine is a made-up name for a synthetic base: no hits in Dolma and no Wikipedia article or mention. Uracil is not one of the four natural DNA bases, so it has no partner in DNA's pairing rule (dna_partner_of covers the natural four) and the new pair fills an empty slot: no natural base is displaced.

In DNA, the base that pairs with vexanin.why: Nobody says whether the partner of a made-up base is in RNA; it follows from the edit and the common fact that uracil is one of the four RNA bases.

notes: ABox expansion paired with biology-replace-0004 (cytosine: guanine to adenine). The revision's new object, adenine, cannot be reused: dna_partner_of is functional and symmetric and adenine's one partner slot already holds thymine, so 'vexanine pairs with adenine' would push thymine out (a hidden revision, not an expansion). Closest non-conflicting expansion: the relation stays dna_partner_of and the made-up subject (the synthetic base vexanine) is paired with uracil, a real base that is not one of the four natural DNA bases and so has no partner in DNA; nothing inherited is overridden. Own questions ask the new value; derived: three 2-hop compositions through it (whether the partner is found in RNA, its one-letter symbol, whether it is a pyrimidine), each through a checked bridge. Unrelated near: cytosine's partner in DNA (guanine), a neighbouring fact the edit leaves alone. The wording never names uracil in the questions.
